character_sheet: A passive ground bird with a fan: a 5x4x11 body on two 7-long stick legs, a raked neck to a small head with a beak, three zero-thickness head-crest feathers and seven zero-thickness 8x30 tail feathers stacked on one pivot (ModelPeacock.java:62-124, sixteen parts). 15 HP, speed 0.38 and an attack attribute of 4 (Peacock.java:38-39, :67-72). It flees monsters within 8 blocks and players within 12 and panics when hurt (:60-62), strolls clear of water (:63), breeds on a crystal apple (:59, :186-188), and on a 1-in-10 tick hunts the nearest termite within 10 blocks, pecking it for a flat 6 within 2 (:141-151); one tick in 5000 it lays one to three spawn eggs (:152-162). Its fan is a timer: a blink state that flips on for 25-125 ticks and off for 50-350 (:40-42, :78-92) opens the seven tail feathers and raises the crest (ModelPeacock.java:135-151). An ambient creature that spawns in the first half of the day between y 50 and 100 with clear air above, at most two others near (:197-204; ModEntities.java:410-411). Read it as a peacock: a stiff strut, a sudden fan, the crest up.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig, x0.5 as a baby (PeacockRenderer.java:28, :40-42; shadow 0.25, :30) on a 128x128 sheet (ModelPeacock.java:126), peacock.png (PeacockRenderer.java:22); the hitbox is 0.65 x 1.2 (ModEntities.java:410-411). The original's ModelPeacock(0.75f) argument was the wingspeed (ModelPeacock.java:21), not a scale. The head crest and the seven tail feathers are zero-thickness planes.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.15 = 0.471 rad (27 deg) x the walking speed above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1, the right leg the negative; 0 below the threshold
groups.plain: the two stick legs swing fore and aft in opposition with the stride
groups.math: a = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 1.3 * 0.75) * pi * 0.15 * amount : 0; lleg.xRot = a; rleg.xRot = -a
groups.phase: the limbSwingAmount threshold of 0.1 gates it
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.3 x 0.75 = 0.975: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.975 = 6.44 ticks

groups.name: fan
groups.axis: x and z (a pose switch, no rhythm)
groups.amplitude: open (blink > 0): every tail feather pitched to 1.047 rad (60 deg) and rolled -0.4 / -0.8 / -1.2 / +0.4 / +0.8 / +1.2 / 0 in order, the crest at 0.401 / -0.174 / -0.698; closed: the tail flat at 0 and the crest folded to -1.06
groups.plain: the tail fans open and the crest rises while the blink timer is on; the tail lies flat and the crest folds when it is off
groups.phase: Peacock.getBlink() (Peacock.java:74-76): a per-side timer field, not a synched byte — on for 25-125 ticks, off for 50-350 (:78-92)
groups.omega_note: no natural period: a pose switch on the blink timer's edges

behaviour: One gait rhythm above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 (ModelPeacock.java:132-134): the two legs swing 27 degrees x the walking speed in opposition at 0.975 rad/tick, a 6.4-tick period, at the 0.38 walk (Peacock.java:38).

One state branch on the blink timer (ModelPeacock.java:135-169; Peacock.java:78-92): while it is on, the seven tail feathers pitch up 60 degrees and splay by 23-degree steps to either side of the centre feather and the three crest feathers rise; while it is off, the tail lies flat behind and the crest folds back at -61 degrees. The timer is a plain field ticked on both sides from each side's own random (:40-42, :78-92), so the fan is not a synched state — a transport for it waits for the SPEC when the rig lands.
The body, neck, head and beak are static; the head does not follow the look. The termite peck (Peacock.java:144-146, a flat 6 within 2 blocks) and the egg (:152-162) draw no pose.
